title: CREATE TABLE
description: Learn how to create a new table in a database with columns, data types, and constraints.

data.text: Tables are used to store data in the database. Each table is uniquely named within a database and schema, and contains one or more columns with associated data types.

data.title: CREATE TABLE Syntax
data.content: Creates a new table with columns, data types, and constraints.
data.code:
CREATE TABLE [database_name.][schema_name.]table_name (
    pk_column data_type PRIMARY KEY,
    column_1 data_type NOT NULL,
    column_2 data_type,
    ...,
    table_constraints
);

items: Specify the database name (optional; defaults to current database) and schema name.
Specify the table name after the schema.
Each column has a name, data type, and optional constraints (NOT NULL, UNIQUE, etc.).
The primary key can be defined inline after a single column or as a table constraint.
Table constraints (FOREIGN KEY, PRIMARY KEY, UNIQUE, CHECK) are defined in the table constraints section.

data.text: The following statement creates a visits table in the sales schema to track customer in-store visits.

data.title: Create Visits Table
data.content: Creates the visits table with columns for customer visits.
data.code:
CREATE TABLE sales.visits (
    visit_id INT PRIMARY KEY IDENTITY (1, 1),
    first_name VARCHAR (50) NOT NULL,
    last_name VARCHAR (50) NOT NULL,
    visited_at DATETIME,
    phone VARCHAR(20),
    store_id INT NOT NULL,
    FOREIGN KEY (store_id) REFERENCES sales.stores (store_id)
);

items: visit_id is the primary key with IDENTITY(1,1) for auto-incrementing values.
first_name and last_name are VARCHAR columns with NOT NULL constraints.
visited_at is a DATETIME column for recording visit timestamps.
phone is a nullable VARCHAR column.
store_id has a FOREIGN KEY constraint referencing the stores table.

data.title: CREATE TABLE Key Points
points: Use CREATE TABLE to define a new table with columns and constraints.
Always specify a primary key for each table.
Use NOT NULL constraints to enforce required values.
FOREIGN KEY constraints ensure referential integrity between tables.
If no database is specified, the table is created in the current database.
